result.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Generating HTML from natural-language specifications is an important application of code large language models (LLMs). Despite producing renderable pages, current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during actual interaction. Existing methods typically target task-specific webpage supervision, leaving demanding interactive artifact optimization underexplored. Using mini-games as a challenging testbed, we expose limitations in interaction experience, reward signal, and credit assignment fidelity that are obscured by shallow webpage interactions. We introduce WebCatalyst, a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework with three complementary components: a game-level GUI assessor for sustained interaction and evaluation, Visual Anchor for mitigating VLM reward hacking, and Action-Trace Credit for grounding token-level credit assignment in runtime execution traces. Trained on fewer than 1K requests, predominantly for games, WebCatalyst raises the Cookie-Bench Mini Games score from 68.8 to 75.3 and also the WebGen-Bench accuracy from 48.8 to 56.9 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, outperforming Claude Opus 4.7 in average rank across evaluated metrics. Further analysis shows that Visual Anchor prevents aesthetic degradation, while runtime-grounded credit assignment accelerates functional improvement. Together, our results show that improving feedback fidelity is the key to substantially advancing interactive HTML generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WebCatalyst 浏览器交互式强化学习框架，以 mini-game 网页生成为测试平台，结合游戏级 GUI 评估器、视觉锚定和基于运行轨迹的动作级 credit assignment，提升生成页面的交互功能与视觉质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「Visual Anchor」缓解 VLM 奖励黑客、以及用执行轨迹做 token 级信用分配，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与轨迹监督的贡献分配提供可核查线索，但研究对象是 HTML 生成而非 latent 推理状态。
